title: Searching
description: Find files by name and search inside file contents.

levels.title: Finding files — find
levels.lesson:
`find` searches the filesystem for files and directories. Its basic form walks a directory tree and prints every path it finds:

```
find /home/user        # list everything under /home/user
find .                 # list everything in the current directory
```

`find` descends into sub-directories automatically — you don't need any flags for that.

challenge.instruction: List every file and directory under `/home/user` using `find`.

levels.title: Searching by name — find -name
levels.lesson:
Add `-name pattern` to filter by filename. Patterns use `*` as a wildcard:

```
find /home/user -name '*.txt'   # every .txt file
find . -name 'README*'          # files starting with README
find / -name 'hosts'            # exact match anywhere
```

Always quote the pattern — the shell would otherwise expand `*` before `find` even sees it.

levels.title: Searching inside files — grep
levels.lesson:
`grep` searches for a **pattern** (text) inside a file and prints every matching line:

```
grep 'error' /var/log/system.log
grep 'localhost' /etc/hosts
```

The first argument is always the pattern; everything after it is a file (or list of files).

When multiple files are given, `grep` prefixes each output line with the filename so you know where the match came from.

levels.title: Searching multiple files — grep
levels.lesson:
Pass several files to `grep` at once and it searches them all:

```
grep 'boot' /var/log/system.log /var/log/error.log
```

When multiple files are given, `grep` prefixes each match with its filename:
```
/var/log/system.log: boot ok
```

This is useful for checking the same pattern across many log files at once.

levels.title: Checkpoint — Searching
levels.lesson: Combine `find` and `grep` to locate and inspect files. Skills covered: `find`, `find -name`, `grep`.

challenge.instruction: First, find all `.txt` files under `/home/user`. Then, search for the word `practice` inside `/home/user/notes.txt`.
